reason: A compound of two shape values, spatulate (PATO_0001937) and oblong (PATO_0000946), handled like ovate-lanceolate in the same review.

label: granulate
definition: A rough quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface being covered with minute, rounded, grain-like elevations. NOTE: Finer than FLOPO:0991088 verruculose; not PATO:0001759 granular, which is a composition quality (containing granules).
reason: A common surface quality of seeds, testas, fruits and spores. PATO granular means containing granules, not a grained surface.
'Densely foliated' stems and shoots bear many leaves along their axes, which is what leafy means. Foliose is already a synonym.

target: new: direction of overlap (imbricate FLOPO:0991063 + left PATO_0000366), stage bud (docs/annotation-context-patterns.md)
reason: This is contort aestivation (how the lobes overlap in bud) with a direction, said of corolla lobes in bud. It combines overlap, a direction and a stage. One term would join three slots.
Strumose (moss capsules) means having a goitre-like swelling on one side at the base. The nearest existing term is gibbous (swollen on one side), so 'not strumose' becomes 'not gibbous'.
Orthotropic stems and shoots grow vertically, as opposed to plagiotropic (sideways-growing) ones. The ovule sense (orthotropous, a straight ovule) is a different quality and is left out of this rule.
'Fruits syncarpes' and 'mericarps syncarp for 66–90%' state that the fruitlets of one flower are fused together. Syncarp is only a noun synonym of fruit in PO.
Ending in two small points: a count of 2 at the apex, like bidentate. It needs 'apiculate' added to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv, with a bearer for the apiculus.
Every example reads 'hypocratériforme' (hypocrateriform, salver-shaped). 'Hypocrepiform' (horseshoe-shaped) is a mistranslation of that word.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (negated surrounding PATO_0001772, towards the buds or flowers)
reason: A relational quality whose second part is given ('the buds', 'the flowers'), stated in the negative.
A disc or calyx 'en collerette' is a narrow ring round the axis or base, which is what ring shaped means (annular).

target: new: two values of one bearer (fimbriated PATO_0002311 and papillose FLOPO:0991059)
reason: Not a continuum: the margin or surface is fringed and papillose at the same time, so both values hold together.
'Not fused' means not fused to the parts being compared, which is what free means. It is handled like 'distinct' and 'separate' (rules C177, C178).
States that the colleter is absent. The colleter class was added in the previous review.
Midrib is an exact synonym of leaf midvein in PO. For mosses, the costa (PO_0030072) also carries 'midrib' as a synonym.
Supra-axillary inflorescences arise above, and so outside, the axil. That is a kind of extra-axillary. Only 7 statements, so a rule is enough.
An everyday word for densely and softly hairy. It is too vague to map to a particular kind of hairiness such as tomentose.

label: buoyant
definition: A buoyancy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's floating in water, its density being less than that of water. NOTE: A disposition of detached fruits, seeds or wood, relevant to dispersal by water; distinct from FLOPO:0991045 floating, the position of a living plant or organ on the water surface.
reason: PATO has only the attribute buoyancy. Buoyant fruits and light wood are recorded traits, and 'specific gravity greater than water' is its negation.
In botany, immaculate means without spots or blotches, i.e. not spotted.

target: new: colour of a marking (banded PATO_0001946, the lines purple PATO_0000951)
reason: The colour belongs to the lines, not to the whole part. It needs the marking and its colour as two linked values.

label: cone-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's architecture resembling a cone (strobilus): a compact, short axis covered with closely imbricate bracts or scales. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991142 spike-like, worded as it is; not PATO:0002021 conical, a geometric shape.
reason: 'Spikes conelike' and 'heads conelike' compare an inflorescence to a strobilus, not to a geometric cone.

target: new: two values of one bearer (reticulate FLOPO:0991100 and sunken PATO_0002416)
reason: A network whose lines are sunk below the surface, so both values hold together. 'Impressed' already maps to sunken (rule C216).
'Invested with/by' only means covered by something. The covering (hairs, perianth, a corky crater) is the real quality, as with 'covered' (C240).
A comparison that does not say what it is compared with, like 'paler' and 'smaller'.
Ending in a distinct point. PATO has 'apiculate' only as a synonym of the attribute sharpness, and mucronate means a short stiff point, so 'pointed' is the safe term.
Floras use 'inversely bell-shaped' with either end as the attachment, and PATO campanulate already widens away from the base. Too rare (6 statements) and unclear for a term.
Calyx-like bracts and perianths look like sepals, as with sepaloid (rule C220).
A costa lamellose at the back bears thin plate-like ridges (lamellae). Lamella itself was rejected as a stand-alone part.
'Not flaring at mouth' and 'base not flaring' (and 'fût sans empattement') negate PATO flared, which means widened outward.

target: new: two values of one bearer (obovate PATO_0001936 and asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: Handled like 'obliquely ovate': the outline is obovate and the sides are unequal, so both values hold together.
